code:
# Rules of engagement, same discipline as a pentest:
#  - in-scope system & environment (named explicitly)
#  - written authorization from the risk owner
#  - time-boxed window
#  - test categories defined BEFORE testing starts
#  - every prompt + response logged as evidence
#
# This is what separates red-teaming from someone
# just "trying to jailbreak the chatbot."
caption: Scope and authorization are what make it a formal assessment, not an attack.

NIST AI 600-1 -> names red-teaming under the "Measure" function
MS AI Red Team + PyRIT -> methodology + open-source test tooling

1. Scope & authorize
2. Design test cases from ATLAS + risk categories
3. Execute & log
4. Report findings with evidence
5. Retest the fix
